sa17:1.2: One time, the Buddha was staying at Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park in Jeta’s Grove of Śrāvastī.
sa17:2.1: There was then a certain monk who rose from his seat.
sa17:2.2: He adjusted his robes to bare his right shoulder and saluted the Buddha with his palms together.
sa17:2.3: He said, “It would be good, Bhagavān, if you were to give me a brief explanation of the Dharma.
sa17:2.4: Having listened to the Dharma, I will go alone to a quiet place, focus on contemplation, and live earnestly.
sa17:2.5: [I’ll then think:] ‘A good son leaves home, cuts off his hair and beard, puts on the Dharma robes, is a believer in the homeless, and leaves home to train on the path.
sa17:2.6: That’s the way he reaches the ultimate and unsurpassed religious practice.
sa17:2.7: He’ll personally realize in the present life:
sa17:2.8: “My births have been ended, the religious practice has been established, and the task has been accomplished.”
sa17:2.9: He himself will know he won’t be subject to a later existence.’”
sa17:3.3: ‘Bhagavān, give me a brief explanation of the Dharma.
sa17:3.4: From that brief explanation of the Dharma, I will get a full understanding of its meaning.
sa17:3.5: I’ll go alone to a quiet place, focus on contemplation, and live earnestly … up to …
sa17:3.6: “He himself knows that he won’t be subject to a later existence.”’
sa17:4.1: The monk said to the Buddha,
sa17:5.2: “Listen closely! Listen closely, and consider it well.
sa17:5.3: I will explain this for you.
sa17:5.4: Monk, you should quickly get rid of something that doesn’t belong to you.
sa17:5.5: Someone who gets rid of that thing will be benefited by this doctrine, and they’ll find happiness for a long time.”
sa17:6.1: That monk then said to the Buddha,
sa17:7.1: The Buddha said to the monk,
sa17:7.2: “How do you understand the meaning of my brief explanation of the Dharma in full?”
sa17:8.1: The monk said to the Buddha,
sa17:8.2: “Bhagavān, form doesn’t belong to me, so I should get rid of it quickly. [Having gotten rid of it, I will be benefited by this doctrine, and I’ll find happiness for a long time.]
sa17:8.3: Feeling … conception … volition … awareness doesn’t belong to me, so I should get rid of it quickly.
sa17:8.4: [Having gotten rid of it,] I will be benefited by this doctrine, and I’ll find happiness for a long time.
sa17:8.5: Therefore, Bhagavān, I understand the meaning of the Bhagavān’s brief explanation of the Dharma in full.”
sa17:9.2: “Good! It’s good, monk, that you understand the meaning of my brief explanation of the Dharma in full.
sa17:9.4: Form doesn’t belong to you, so you should get rid of it quickly. [Having gotten rid of it, you will be benefited by this doctrine, and you’ll find happiness for a long time.]
sa17:9.5: Thus, feeling … conception … volition … awareness doesn’t belong to you, so you should get rid of it quickly.
sa17:9.6: [Having gotten rid of it,] you will be benefited by this doctrine, and you’ll find happiness for a long time.”
sa17:10.1: When that monk heard what the Buddha taught, he felt great joy.
sa17:10.2: He bowed to the Buddha and withdrew.
sa17:10.3: He then went alone to a quiet place where he diligently trained and lived earnestly.
sa17:10.4: After diligently training and living earnestly, he thought,
sa17:10.5: “A good son leaves home, cuts off his hair and beard, puts on the Dharma robes, believes at home in being homeless, and leaves home … up to …
sa17:10.6: He himself knows that he won’t be subject to a later existence.”
sa17:11.1: That monk then became an arhat, and his mind was liberated.
